scope: Move the existing native Session integral codec into fsym-core while preserving its public facade and version1 wire format
Expose native and Python integral receipt export and receiver-bound independent replay
Share original-source, typed-axis, exact-rational and declared-assumption admission between public generation and replay
Retain canonical Abs class identity, immutable receipt ownership, cumulative budgets and final cancellation checks
trust_boundary: Exact built-in bytes at most1MiB are admitted before expected-source conversion. The receiver's original source, typed variable, ordered bounds, tolerance and context must match before bounded witness decoding. Only independent core quadrature grants a receipt; stored acceptance flags, cached enclosures and adaptive regeneration are not used.
compatibility: The moved Session codec retains its schema version, field order, byte encoding, arithmetic charges and public root facade. Immediate IntegrationError causes remain visible to typed host error mapping. Cross-interface exchange requires the same exact source representation and context; Python source-only Abs tags retain the closed built-in class.
limits: Proper finite real integration only; existing quadrature grammar, input-height, partition and precision caps remain. The public API has one cumulative caller ledger without a separately reserved verifier pool. No pickle or arbitrary Python object is decoded.

validation.independent_math_oracle: Isolated SymPy1.14.0 verified all7 exact polynomial/absolute-value fixtures used by core acceptance tests, including reversed and equal endpoints. This is fixture evidence only.
validation.independent_review: Core codec compared with the prior Session implementation; field order, charge amounts/order, source binding before witness decoding and the final checker boundary are preserved. Two agents reviewed native GIL-detach ownership, cumulative fallback capture, public exact-input admission, typed errors and all30 public cases; no concrete defect found.
validation.python_ast: Passed for the changed public shell modules and both new public integral test modules.
validation.rustfmt: Passed formatting and --check on all 13 changed/new Rust paths, including the final bridge, mapper, core codec, facade/tests and three prior optimizer files. Used rustfmt 1.10.0-nightly (f7d782a3be 2026-08-19), recovered from checksum-verified official nightly-2026-08-20 archives after the host reset. The final pass changed no bytes.
validation.whitespace: git diff --check passed on the complete implementation, tests and documentation changes.
validation.candidate_execution: Rust and actual-extension tests remain unexecuted. Earlier compiler attempts repeatedly lost the host or were SIGKILLed; no Cargo build was repeated in this continuation.
validation.ci: New core transport tests, mapper tests and public transport cases are selected by the existing native and actual-extension CI suites. No remote pass is claimed.

adjacent_numeric_validation: Pinned formatting repaired three existing optimizer transport/search files from the preceding commit. Earlier11 changed Python files passed AST parsing. These are syntax/format evidence only and do not convert pending optimizer runtime validation into a pass.
claims: No workstream, campaign, compatibility, performance or certification gate is closed or promoted.
